steps.instruction: In the Properties panel on the right, click the Render tab (the camera-back icon, second from the top).
steps.spoken: In the column of small icons on the right, click the second one. It looks like the back of a camera.
steps.why: Render settings control how your final picture is made.
steps.hint_if_stuck: It is the second icon from the top, under the tools icon.

steps.instruction: Look at Render Engine. This is the program that draws your picture.
steps.spoken: Render Engine is the artist that paints your picture. EEVEE is fast, Cycles is slower but more realistic.
steps.why: Fast engines are good for previews. Realistic engines are good for final images.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Render Engine is the first setting at the top of the Render tab.

steps.instruction: Find Sampling. More samples means a cleaner picture but a longer wait.
steps.spoken: Sampling is how many times Blender looks at each dot. More looks give a cleaner picture but take longer.
steps.why: It is a trade between quality and waiting time.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Sampling is the first section under Render Engine.
